record.paper_title: The Branch-Cut Cosmology: evidences and open questions
record.original_question: If the branch-cut scale factor shrinks only to a finite critical size well above the Planck limit, what is the physical nature of the finite-size transition between the primordial contraction phase and the primordial expansion phase, which the authors describe as a classical leap?

evidence.quote: This finite size limitation of the range, well above the Planck limit, implies in the branch-cut cosmology (de Freitas Pacheco et al., 2023) a leap, of a classical nature, between the primordial phases of contraction and expansion, a topic that needs further investigation in the future.

artifact.self_contained_problem: Consider a cosmological model in which the scale factor a(t) is replaced by a complex-analytic function defined on a Riemann surface with a branch cut, so that the usual singular contraction to a = 0 is replaced by a minimal modulus |a| = a_min that is strictly greater than the Planck length ℓ_P. Assume the cosmological evolution proceeds along a path on this Riemann surface that descends from a primordial contracting branch (with da/dt < 0) to the value a_min and then continues onto an expanding branch (da/dt > 0), with the transition occurring at a finite, non-Planckian scale.\n\nQuestion: Provide a rigorous physical and mathematical characterization of the finite-size transition between the contracting and expanding branches at a = a_min. In particular, determine whether this transition can be described as a classical (non-quantum) leap, identify the appropriate matching conditions for the metric and matter fields across the branch cut, and specify the dynamical equations and conserved quantities that govern this transition.
artifact.status_search_result: The branch-cut cosmology framework explicitly states that the finite-size classical leap between contraction and expansion phases requires further investigation; no published resolution has been located. The question remains an open research direction within this cosmological model.

status_evidence.title: The Branch-Cut Cosmology: evidences and open questions
status_evidence.snippet: This finite size limitation of the range, well above the Planck limit, implies ... a leap, of a classical nature, between the primordial phases of contraction and expansion, a topic that needs further investigation in the future.
status_evidence.claim: The nature of the contraction-to-expansion transition is identified as an open problem requiring future investigation.
